newsitem.title: USA: Ionic Fuel sees higher revs in fiscal 1997.
newsitem.headline: Ionic Fuel sees higher revs in fiscal 1997.

text.p: Ionic Fuel Technology Inc said Wednesday it expected "sharply higher" revenues in the 1997 fiscal year after signing two deals to install its combustion and emissions system at two oil facilities.

Ionic Fuel, which develops systems to improve combustion efficiency and reduce emissions of fuels like oil, said it had received orders from "a U.S. oil company for its U.K. site and a major refiner in the Czech Republic".
It said it was also negotiating with other major international refiners in the British and Europe to cover six operating sites.
"From these developments, the company expects substantially higher revenues in fiscal (1997) ... resulting in a positive cash flow and a profitable level of operations," it said.
Its chairman, Douglas Johnston, told Reuters the negotiations with the other refiners had been going on for the past few months.
"We hope they will end soon," he said, without elaborating.

The company said the orders for its IFT System came after test trials at a British research center showed it improved combustion of fuels, lowered emissions, and removed "coke" on the fireside surfaces of a plant.
Ionic Fuel, an environmental and combustion technology company, reported a share loss of $0.29 for the 1996 fiscal year ended June 30 against a share loss of $0.51 for the previous fiscal year.
Although it is based in Wilmington, Delaware, it has a manufacturing facilities in Laindon, Essex, England and a marketing and sales focus in Britain and Europe.
